title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Endobronchial Valves for Persistent Air Leak and Bronchopleural Fistula in Children: A Systematic Review of Indications, Procedural Approaches, and Outcomes.
authors: Mahindrakar N, Bhandari P, Yedatore R, Vorakunthada Y, Lilitwat W
abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent air leak (PAL) and bronchopleural fistula (BPF) are uncommon but important complications in children, particularly with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative injury, malignancy, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). When conservative therapy fails or surgery is high-risk, endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement has emerged as a minimally invasive bronchoscopic option. This systematic review summarizes the published pediatric experience, focusing on indications, procedural approach, and outcomes. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 2026, with Google Scholar and reference lists screened; no language limits applied. Eligible studies reported pediatric or late-adolescent patients who underwent bronchoscopic valve placement for PAL, BPF, or pneumothorax with ongoing air leak. Case reports, case series, and observational studies with extractable pediatric data were included. Two reviewers independently screened, assessed eligibility, and abstracted data; findings were synthesized narratively. RESULTS: Thirteen reports were included. Valve placement achieved rapid or eventual air-leak improvement in selected children, including those with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative air leak, chronic ventilator dependence, malignancy, and ECMO support. Reported complications included valve migration or loosening, granulation tissue, minor hemoptysis, atelectasis, contralateral pneumothorax, and recurrent air leak, although many children underwent valve removal without complication. CONCLUSION: Endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement may be a useful rescue or bridge therapy for carefully selected children with refractory PAL or BPF. Evidence remains low certainty owing to small samples, retrospective design, inconsistent outcome definitions, and possible publication bias. Prospective multicenter registries with standardized reporting are needed to define optimal selection, timing, and safety.

title: Predicting IGD treatment outcomes across interventions using a whole-brain functional connectome biomarker.
authors: Wei M, Luo X, Fu J, Li S, Ni H, Liu J, Dong GH
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although treatment approaches have been explored in internet gaming disorder (IGD), however, little is known about the specific neural activity that is associated with treatment outcomes. This study aims to establish a treatment-sensitive network that reliably predicts treatment outcomes across different interventions for IGD. METHODS: Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 90 individuals with IGD who received one of three different intervention protocols (mindfulness meditation, approach bias modification, or retrieval-aversive conditioning training). Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM) was used to build a treatment-sensitive network to predict individual symptom reduction, then validated them on the external dataset. RESULTS: The negative (r = 0.401, p <.001) and combined network (r = 0.480, p <.001) can significantly predict a reduction of addiction severity (baseline minus post-test). Specifically, the negative network was primarily centred on the motor, subcortical, and salience networks. The positive network primarily involved cerebellar-related connections. Incorporating these into a combined model significantly improved predictive accuracy, suggesting that cerebellar-related connectivity may contribute to the prediction of intervention-related clinical improvement. Finally, the treatment-sensitive network was validated in a separate data. CONCLUSIONS: This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: The trial protocol was pre-registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn; ChiCTR2300077831(MM), ChiCTR2300075869(ApBm), ChiCTR2500095444(R-AC), ChiCTR2400090834(SAE)).

title: Engineering biomaterials to improve cytokine therapies for wound healing.
authors: Horton I, Maisel K, Sadtler K
abstract: Recombinant cytokines have been used as therapeutics for cancers, autoimmune diseases, and infectious diseases, but their application in wound healing and tissue regeneration remains relatively underdeveloped. Short half-lives, narrow therapeutic windows, and a myriad of adverse effects due to pleiotropy and redundancy have limited their clinical use. Biomaterial-based delivery platforms such as hydrogels, particles, and scaffolds have gained traction as engineering strategies to bridge this translational gap. Despite their popularity in preclinical research, the last FDA approved biomaterial-based cytokine therapeutic, becaplermin, was approved in 1997. Unlike reviews that focus on material design alone, we investigate clinical trials from 2012 to present day and look at the barriers and bottlenecks of translating this technology beyond the bench. This review focuses on release kinetics, design parameters, and practical applications of cytokine-loaded hydrogels, particles, and scaffolds to accelerate wound healing and regenerate functional tissue after soft tissue damage. We offer insights about future directions for preclinical testing and further engineering considerations to aid in their translation to clinical care for patients with soft tissue injuries.

title: Contraception during the transition to menopause: a commentary.
authors: Versailles JBE, Bahamondes L, Grandi G, Juliato CRT
journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The transition to menopause presents unique clinical challenges, requiring a balance between pregnancy prevention and the management of perimenopausal symptoms and age-related comorbidities. Although fertility declines with advancing age, unintended pregnancy after age 40 remains possible and is associated with increased maternal and neonatal risks. Women who wish to avoid pregnancy need effective contraception until menopause is established. OBJECTIVE: To provide practical guidance on contraceptive counselling during the transition to menopause, considering the safety, effectiveness, noncontraceptive benefits, and limitations of available contraceptive methods. RESULTS: Age alone is not a contraindication to any contraceptive method; however, the higher prevalence of cardiovascular, metabolic, and malignant conditions in this population requires individualised contraceptive counselling based on each woman's medical history, preferences, reproductive goals, and shared decision-making. Contraceptive care in midlife is more complex than pregnancy prevention alone. Contraceptive counselling should consider both the likelihood of user adherence and the noncontraceptive benefits of each method. CONCLUSION: This commentary provides practical guidance on contraceptive counselling during the transition to menopause, reviewing the safety, effectiveness, noncontraceptive benefits, and limitations of both short-acting reversible contraceptives (SARCs) and long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) to support informed, individualised contraceptive care.

title: A let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicle-laden bioactive scaffold promotes immunomodulation and regeneration of segmental tracheal defects.
authors: Liu B, Wei N, Liang L, Shi Z, Liu P, Zeng T, Zhang H, Zhang H
abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. Persistent post-injury inflammation, inadequate neovascularization, and delayed epithelial restoration contribute to the formation of granulation tissue and subsequent graft failure. In this study, we developed a bioactive tracheal scaffold for sustained local delivery of let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicles (let-7a-5p-EVs) to modulate the regenerative microenvironment during tracheal repair. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In a rabbit segmental tracheal defect model, the let-7a-5p-EV-laden scaffold enhanced neovascularization, mitigated local inflammatory responses, promoted mucociliary epithelial reconstruction, and maintained airway patency. The let-7a-5p-EV scaffold improved biomechanical recovery, and increased survival rates. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation indicated that these effects were associated with the attenuation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-associated inflammatory activation, as evidenced by reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. These findings demonstrate that sustained local delivery of engineered EVs from a mechanically competent bioactive scaffold provides an effective immunomodulatory strategy for the regenerative repair of segmental tracheal defects and offers translational potential for functional airway reconstruction.

title: Rapid and visual detection of group B Streptococcus based on an ERA-CasMNPs colorimetric biosensor.
authors: Guo H, Jiang Y, Li D, He K, Chen Y, Li Y, Dai S, He Y
abstract: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is a major pathogen responsible for adverse perinatal outcomes; rapid and accurate detection is crucial for preventing maternal-neonatal transmission and for guiding clinical interventions. Current GBS detection methods are limited by long assay times, insufficient sensitivity, and high equipment and operational requirements, restricting their application in resource-limited settings and rapid detection scenarios. Targeting the cfb gene of GBS, this study developed ERA-CasMNPs by integrating enzymatic recombinase amplification (ERA), CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated specific recognition and trans-cleavage activity of ssDNA, and horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-modified magnetic nanoparticle complexes (MNPs)-based colorimetric signal output. The ERA-CasMNPs biosensor enables rapid and sensitive visual detection of GBS within 85 min, with an LOD95 of 23.3 copies/μL (95% confidence interval: 15.6-34.8 copies/μL). Moreover, evaluation using 135 cultured clinical bacterial isolates demonstrated that ERA-CasMNPs achieved a sensitivity of 97.33%, a specificity of 98.33%, and a detection accuracy of 97.78%, comparable to qPCR. These results indicate that the ERA-CasMNPs biosensor provides a sensitive and visual method for rapid detection of GBS and supports its potential for further evaluation in resource-limited and rapid-testing settings.

title: Atypical early-life ultrasonic vocalizations disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad in the BTBR model of autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Cofsky NI, Binder MS
abstract: Alterations in early-life communication are a defining feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). While these deficits are well conserved in mouse models, few studies have assessed how aberrations in neonatal vocalizations affect maternal behaviors and disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad. To better elucidate the consequences of altered communication in ASD models, we assessed ultrasonic vocalization (USV) production in pups and the corresponding retrieval behaviors in dams using C57 and BTBR (autistic-like) mice. We first used the pup's dam as the retriever and found that BTBR dams retrieved significantly fewer pups than C57 dams. We then used a novel C57 dam as the retriever and found that BTBR pups were retrieved significantly slower than C57 pups. Follow-up analyses detected positive correlations between call duration and retrieval time and amplitude and retrieval time in BTBR pups. Similarly, we found that C57 mice that were retrieved the fastest had calls of a lower amplitude than slowly retrieved mice. In the BTBR model, we found that faster retrieved mice produced shorter calls with a higher pitch than slowly retrieved mice, displaying call characteristics more similar to C57 pups. Lastly, we found that a more diverse call type repertoire was associated with a faster retrieval time. Overall, our study demonstrates that altered USV production significantly affects the pup-dam communication dyad. Furthermore, we identified the USV duration, amplitude, and a more diverse call type repertoire as being critical factors underlying maternal retrieval.

title: Postoperative infections after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass - incidence, performance of diagnostic procedures, and predictive factors.
authors: Erixon C, Johannesson E, Dardashti A, Melhammar L, Nilsson J, Thelaus L, Linder A, Zindovic I
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cardiac surgery using cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) induces a systemic inflammatory response that affects common inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP), white blood cell count (WBC), and body temperature, complicating postoperative diagnosis of infections. The objective of this study was to assess the incidence of postoperative infections and evaluate the performance of clinically used biomarkers. DESIGN: This was a bidirectional cohort study including patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB between 1st of February 2020 and 22nd of September 2021. Patients with postoperative infection were compared to patients without. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of postoperative infections. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated the diagnostic ability of current biomarkers to detect infection. RESULTS: A total of 1,222 patients were included. The incidence of postoperative infections (during hospitalisation and/or late infection) was 17.3%. Patients with postoperative infection had more comorbidities, underwent more complex procedures, and had higher mortality (90-day mortality 3.8% vs 1.5%, p = 0.045; 1-year mortality 5.7% vs 2.7%, p = 0.032). CRP, WBC, and temperature performed poorly in detecting postoperative infection, although peak CRP (OR 1.069, p < 0.001) and peak temperature (OR 2.408, p = 0.005) were independent predictors of postoperative infection. Peak temperature occurred on postoperative day 5 in infected patients versus day 2 in those without infection. CONCLUSION: Postoperative infections following cardiac surgery with CPB remain common and are associated with increased postoperative complications and mortality. Common inflammatory biomarkers perform poorly in detecting infection. Improved diagnostic tools are needed to facilitate early detection and treatment.

title: Enhanced Esophageal Cancer Detection Using Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer: A Comparative Study of White Light Imaging, Narrow-Band Imaging, and Algorithmic Narrow-Band Imaging-Like Imaging.
authors: Wu JW, Wang YK, Mukundan A, Karmakar R, Nhu NNQ, Nagisetti Y, Liao WC, Han ML
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) detection is crucial for improving survival. While narrow-band imaging (NBI) improves mucosal visualization, limitations remain. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer (SAVE), an algorithmic NBI-like technology reconstructed from white light imaging (WLI). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, image-based exploratory feasibility study to descriptively evaluate the diagnostic performance of WLI, NBI, and SAVE. A dataset of 1350 still endoscopic images (450 each for WLI, NBI, and SAVE) across normal mucosa, dysplasia, and ESCC stages from 158 patients was blindly reviewed by three endoscopists with different experience levels (3, 5, and 15 years). Diagnostic metrics included sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and reading time. RESULTS: For ESCC, SAVE demonstrated diagnostic performance metrics (sensitivity: 0.81-0.97, specificity: 0.85-0.96) that were numerically similar to WLI and NBI. For dysplasia detection, SAVE had lower observed sensitivity (0.39-0.62) compared to NBI (0.55-0.85) across all observers, representing a clinical limitation for precancerous screening in its current format. Mean per-image reading times were similar across WLI, NBI, and SAVE. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study, SAVE showed diagnostic potential for ESCC, with observed diagnostic performance metrics numerically similar to those of WLI and NBI in this exploratory dataset, but lacked sensitivity for dysplasia. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant further prospective, multicenter validation to refine the algorithm for early cancer detection.

title: Acute Pancreatitis Caused by Impaction of Migrated Surgical Staples in the Duodenal Papilla After Distal Pancreatectomy.
authors: Inaba K, Motomura M, Azuma Y, Kimoto T, Takahashi H, Ueo T, Narita R, Tada K
abstract: A 67-year-old woman underwent a laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy for pancreatic body cancer. On postoperative day (POD) 23, the patient presented with epigastric pain and was diagnosed with delayed peripancreatic fluid collection, which was treated with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage. On POD 51, the patient developed recurrent epigastric pain. Laboratory tests revealed elevated pancreatic enzyme and inflammatory marker levels. Computed tomography revealed acute pancreatitis and a high-density area in the duodenal papilla suggestive of a foreign body. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography revealed that the surgical staples were impacted in the minor duodenal papilla and were successfully removed. Although pancreatography did not demonstrate residual staples, three additional staples were subsequently removed from the pancreatic duct. Pancreatitis improved after endoscopic treatment, and the patient was discharged. This case suggests that the migration of staples used during surgery may be a contributing factor to postoperative pancreatitis.

title: Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Gastric-Type Mucosal Lesions in Non-Ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors Based on Mucin Phenotype.
authors: Ohno K, Nakatani E, Kurokami T, Kawai A, Matsuda M, Masui Y, Satoh T, Hirata T
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors differ in clinicopathological features according to mucin phenotype. Gastric-type tumors have distinct biological features; however, their associated mucosal background remains unclear. In this study, gastric foveolar metaplasia, gastric heterotopia, and Brunner's gland hyperplasia were collectively referred to as gastric-type mucosal lesions (G-MLs). We aimed to assess their prevalence and associations with mucin phenotype and clinicopathological factors. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the data of 130 patients with 130 resected non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors at a single center. Tumors were classified according to mucin phenotype. The prevalence of concomitant G-MLs and associated factors was evaluated. Exploratory Firth-penalized logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between gastric-type tumors and G-ML presence. RESULTS: Concomitant G-MLs were identified in 44 patients (33.8%). Their prevalence was higher in gastric-type tumors (13/16; 81.3%) than in gastric-intestinal-type tumors (10/37; 27.0%) and intestinal-type tumors (21/77; 27.3%). G-MLs were associated with mild endoscopic gastric mucosal atrophy and smoking status and were inversely associated with current Helicobacter pylori infection. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, gastric-type tumors remained positively associated with the presence of G-MLs (adjusted odds ratio, 7.00; 95% confidence interval, 1.98-30.95; p = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: G-MLs were present in approximately one-third of patients and were most frequent in gastric-type tumors. These findings indicate an association between G-MLs and gastric-type tumors; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow inference of a biological relationship. TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

Long-term Endoscopic Evolution of a Pyloric Gland Adenoma Arising in Nonatrophic Gastric Mucosa and Initially Resembling a Fundic Gland Polyp.
authors: Kobayashi R, Nakanishi H, Takaura K, Tanaka S, Maeyashiki C, Tamaki N, Yasui Y, Sakurai U
abstract: Pyloric gland adenoma (PGA) is a rare gastric epithelial neoplasm often associated with autoimmune or metaplastic atrophic gastritis. An 80-year-old man underwent serial upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. A small gastric fundus lesion initially resembling a fundic gland polyp (FGP) was followed without biopsy. Over 11 years, it enlarged to 22 mm and became increasingly whitish, against a background described endoscopically as nonatrophic. Biopsy suggested PGA, and the lesion was resected en bloc by endoscopic submucosal dissection. Closely packed pyloric-type glands showed elongation, tortuosity, branching, and cystic dilatation, with diffuse MUC6 expression and MUC5AC expression restricted to the surface epithelium. The lesion was diagnosed as PGA with low-grade dysplasia. The adjacent oxyntic mucosa showed no atrophy, lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, or nodular enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia. Without an initial biopsy, whether the lesion was already PGA or developed within a pre-existing FGP remains unknown. An enlarging or increasingly whitish FGP-like lesion warrants histologic assessment, even in nonatrophic gastric mucosa.

title: Hybrid nanovesicle artificial antigen-presenting cells integrate endogenous tumor antigen display with senescence-mimetic erythrocyte membrane-directed splenic T-cell priming.
authors: Yang Z, Li S, Guo Y, Wang T, Han H, Ma M, Zhang Y, Tang W
abstract: Artificial antigen-presenting cells (aAPCs) provide a non-genetic approach to T-cell activation, but their in vivo performance is often limited by predefined peptide-major histocompatibility complex class I (pMHC-I) repertoires and inefficient delivery to secondary lymphoid organs. Here, we engineer senescence-derived hybrid nanovesicles that integrate endogenous antigen display and organ-directed trafficking within a single membrane material. Nanovesicles derived from senescent cancer cells retain increased levels of endogenously generated pMHC-I complexes, whereas nanovesicles derived from senescence-mimetic red blood cells confer spleen-directed biodistribution. Fusion of these membranes generates SS-hNVs, which are further functionalized with anti-CD28 and interleukin-2 to form SS-aAPCs that provide coordinated T-cell receptor (TCR), costimulatory, and cytokine signals. Hybrid membrane composition governs splenic accumulation and CD8+ T-cell engagement following intravenous administration. SS-aAPCs expand antigen-specific CD8+ T cells and TCF-1+PD-1+ progenitor-like populations, enhance cytotoxic responses, and suppress tumor growth in B16-OVA and MC38 models. Combination with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) blockade further improves tumor control. By assigning endogenous antigen display and lymphoid trafficking to distinct source membranes, this platform establishes a structure-function strategy for constructing systemically administered aAPCs. These findings support that physiologically remodeled membranes can be assembled as modular biomaterials to coordinate molecular immune signaling with organ-level biodistribution, enabling in vivo T-cell priming without predefined epitope loading or genetic modification of immune cells.

title: Thermosensitive and tumor-targeted asparaginase fusion protein enables metabolic-immunotherapy for solid tumors.
authors: Gong L, Wang X, Zheng Y, Liu S, Zhang F, Sun Y, Qi Y, Han L
abstract: Metabolic therapies targeting tumor amino acid dependence, represented by asparaginase (ASNase), have shown limited efficacy in solid tumors, owing to poor stability, low penetration, and high immunogenicity. Here, we design a thermosensitive tumor-targeted ASNase fusion protein (ASNase-ELP-LHRH) via AlphaFold2, by integrating elastin-like polypeptide (ELP) and luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH), to overcome these drawbacks. ELP drives in situ depot formation, extending half-life to ∼400 h (95-fold increase) and reducing anti-ASNase antibody levels 70-fold. LHRH mediates receptor-dependent tumor targeting and deep penetration. ASNase-ELP-LHRH achieves persistent asparagine (Asn) depletion, counteracting metabolic adaptation to induce nutrient starvation and apoptosis. Mechanistically, the construct blocks metastasis by suppressing epithelial-mesenchymal transition through downregulating Twist1 and upregulating E-cadherin, effectively inhibiting lung metastasis for 25 days in triple-negative breast cancer models. We further observed time-dependent changes in CD8+ T-cell effector-marker expression under Asn deprivation, characterized by dynamic alterations in IFN-γ and granzyme B expression. Combined with anti-PD-L1, this achieves a "dual boost" of antitumor immunity, durably inhibiting metastasis for 40 days and extending survival 1.5-fold. The modular ligand-exchangeable platform offers a generalizable strategy for protein optimization and establishes ASNase-ELP-LHRH as a promising metabolic-immunotherapeutic agent for solid tumors, bridging protein engineering, tumor metabolism and cancer immunology.

Adolescent social isolation drives sex-dependent shifts in medial prefrontal cortex endocannabinoid tone and excitatory/inhibitory balance: the protective role of a methyl donor.
authors: Ricciardi F, Mosca L, Belardo C, Bonsale R, Fusco A, Teweldemedhin MM, Piscitelli F, di Marzo V
abstract: Prolonged social isolation triggers neuropsychiatric impairments linked to brain neurotransmitter imbalances. This study investigated the impact of social isolation on sensory perception, affective states, and the levels of amino acid neurotransmitters and endocannabinoids within the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) of both male and female adolescent mice. Furthermore, we evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe), a methyl donor with established antidepressant properties, in mitigating these alterations. Single-housed (SH) male mice developed mechanical allodynia, cold hyperalgesia, depression-like behavior, and general malaise, alongside significantly decreased GABA levels in the mPFC. SAMe treatment effectively ameliorated these symptoms, restoring GABAergic tone and increasing glycine and glutamate levels. In contrast, SH female mice exhibited anxiety-like behavior and pain hypersensitivity without depression-like traits. Their neurochemical profile was characterized by decreased GABA but increased levels of glutamate and specific endocannabinoids/acylethanolamides (2-AG, PEA, and LEA) in the mPFC. In females, SAMe treatment successfully reversed anxiety-like behavior and pain hypersensitivity, normalized glutamate, LEA, and GABA levels, and increased glycine and DHG. Our findings demonstrate that while social isolation-induced neuropsychiatric and neurochemical alterations are sex-dependent, the development of sensory hypersensitivity and the therapeutic responsiveness to SAMe are consistent across sexes. By restoring GABAergic homeostasis and modulating excitatory and endocannabinoid signaling in the mPFC, SAMe emerges as a promising pharmacological intervention for treating the complex psychiatric and sensory sequelae induced by chronic social stress.

title: Children's health before, during, and after parental/caregiver immigration detention in the United States: findings from a cross-sectional survey.
authors: Thapa K, Patler C, Saadi A
abstract: BACKGROUND: Parental immigration detention is a significant yet understudied stressor with potential consequences for children's well-being. We examined children's general health before, during, and after parental detention, and compared to the United States (US) pediatric population. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional household telephone survey in 2022-2023 of family members of immigrants detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in 2020/21 and released on bond. Of 88 respondents, we analyzed data from 49 families with at least one school-aged minor child. Family members retrospectively reported on child health before, during, and after detention using the 7-item parent-report version of the PROMIS® Parent Proxy Scale- Global Health 7 measure, which provides standardized T-scores (mean = 50, SD = 10) benchmarked to the U.S. general population. FINDINGS: The mean T-scores were statistically equivalent to the population mean of 50 at pre-detention (49; 95% CI: 46.0, 52.0) and after release (48.9; 95% CI: 45.5, 52.4) but 17 T-score points (∼2 SD below the population mean) lower during detention (31.8; 95% CI: 28.6, 35.0), substantially exceeding the commonly accepted 5 T-score points threshold (half-SD) for clinically meaningful change. Reported problems for children during parental detention included decline in grades (n = 34, 69%), increased financial responsibilities (n = 29, 59%), household or caregiving responsibilities (n = 26, 53%), and food insecurity (n = 26, 53%). About 16% (n = 8) of children were unable to receive needed treatment or counseling from a mental health professional during parental detention. INTERPRETATION: Parental detention was associated with poorer reported child health, and reported health scores improved after release. Findings highlight the need for policies that consider the health consequences of immigration enforcement on children and families. FUNDING: This research was supported by the National Science Foundation and the Russell Sage Foundation and the Carnegie Corporation of New York.

title: N-acetylcysteine decreases toluene conditioned place preference and modulates corticostriatal activity in adolescent rats.
authors: Carampel AC, Asis JLB, Munar JC, Gregorio CGC, Medina PMB, Quirk GJ, Cena-Navarro R
abstract: Inhalant (toluene) use disorder (IUD) continues to be a public health problem especially among Filipino adolescents. Animal models of IUD have not yet explored neurobiological changes from chronic toluene exposure, or possible treatments for long-lasting toluene-induced deficits. In rats repeatedly exposed to 3000 ppm of toluene vapor over 12 days, we report that daily administration of N-acetylcysteine (NACys; 100 mg/kg i.p. or 0.9 g/l oral), but not melatonin (10 mg/kg i.p.), during 8 days of abstinence reduced toluene conditioned place preference in both male and female adolescent Sprague Dawley rats. Using immunofluorescence, we found that toluene-exposed rats showed decreased c-Fos densities in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), dorsolateral striatum, and ventrolateral orbitofrontal cortex (vlOFC) after 8 days of abstinence. NACys partially rescued c-Fos expression in vlOFC. We found that c-Fos densities in both vlOFC and prelimbic cortex were significantly correlated with CPP values and with c-Fos densities in the DMS across treatment groups, suggesting that a history of toluene exposure may act by reducing cortical modulation of the dorsal striatum to promote long-lasting drug context seeking. Our findings suggest that NACys may be a promising treatment for IUD in adolescent males and females.

title: Maternal piromelatine treatment is associated with attenuated behavioral alterations and sex-specific changes in hippocampal pCREB/BDNF signaling in adult offspring following prenatal constant-light exposure.
authors: Stoyanova T, Ivanova P, Tchekalarova J
abstract: Maternal exposure to constant light during pregnancy (CLE) is associated with disrupted circadian organization and persistent behavioral alterations in adult offspring. This study examined behavioural performance and 24-hour locomotor activity patterns, as well as hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels, in adult male and female offspring following prenatal CLE and maternal treatment with piromelatine (pir), which acts as an agonist at melatonin MT1/MT2 and serotonin 5-HT1A/5-HT1D receptors. Pregnant Wistar rats under light-dark regime received vehicle (veh), whereas dams exposed to CLE received vehicle (LL-veh), pir (10 mg/kg), or melatonin. Compared to the LL-veh groups, offspring from pir-treated dams exhibited reduced anxiety- and depression-like responses and improved working memory in both sexes. Individual-subject cosinor analysis revealed heterogeneous 24-hour locomotor rhythmicity within and between groups. No significant treatment-group effect was detected for MESOR or amplitude, and the descriptive acrophase patterns did not provide evidence of treatment-induced restoration or normalization of circadian organization. Maternal pir treatment was associated with higher hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels in male, but not female offspring relative to the LL-veh group. While the behavioral and molecular differences occurred concurrently in males, these findings do not prove that pCREB/BDNF signaling mediated the behavioral outcomes. Furthermore, the study cannot distinguish the direct developmental effects of maternal pir exposure from those mediated through maternal or offspring circadian rhythm. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as long-term behavioral and sex-specific molecular differences associated with maternal pir treatment rather than as evidence of circadian-independent antidepressant, anxiolytic, cognitive-enhancing, or BDNF-enhancing actions.

title: Functional remodeling of the maternal brain: Linking brain c-Fos dynamics to behavioral changes in pregnancy: An exploratory study.
authors: Yang L, Shang Y, Liu X, Wang J, Zhang H, Yang L
abstract: As an exploratory study with a limited sample size, this work systematically examined pregnancy-induced changes in neural activity by analyzing c-Fos expression across the whole brain of pregnant mice. The results showed that 36 brain regions-including the cortex, hippocampus, thalamus, and hypothalamus-exhibited dynamic changes in c-Fos expression throughout pregnancy. Behavioral tests revealed that pregnant mice displayed increased anxiety-like behavior in the elevated plus maze. Group-level descriptive correlation analysis indicated nominal directional trends between regional c-Fos expression and anxiety-related behavior, but no associations remained statistically significant after multiple testing correction. Furthermore, comparison with human prenatal brain imaging data suggested that adaptive changes in the hippocampus and hypothalamus are conserved across species. These preliminary findings provide initial insights into understanding brain adaptation during pregnancy, and require validation in larger cohort studies.

title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor use in third trimester of pregnancy and birth outcomes after vaginal birth - a Swedish retrospective register study 2005-2015.
authors: Thies-Lagergren L, Hildingsson I, Johansson M
journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are prescribed for depression during pregnancy, yet the impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes remains insufficiently studied. The study aimed to describe the prevalence of prescribed SSRIs to pregnant women and its association with birth outcomes after a vaginal birth. METHODS: A registry study included 405,936 term vaginal births in Sweden. SSRI prescriptions were identified. Crude and adjusted odds ratios with 99% confidence intervals were calculated, with statistical significance set at p < 0.001. RESULTS: SSRIs were prescribed to 6.374 women (1.6%), with prevalence rising from 0.3% to 2.6% between 2005 and 2015. SSRI was associated with significantly higher rates of labor induction, epidural anesthesia and PPH > 1000 mL. postpartum. Women prescribed SSRIs were more likely to give birth at 37-38 weeks' gestation and have neonates with head circumference < 35 cm and with Apgar score < 7 at 5 min. CONCLUSIONS: SSRI prescriptions increased significantly between 2005 and 2015 and were associated with higher risks of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Until more conclusive evidence is availble midwives and obstetricians should remain vigilant when supporting pregnant women with depression or anxiety, considering the potential risks of pharmacological treatment alongside non-pharmacological management of maternal mental health conditions.

title: The severity of preeclampsia in naturally conceived versus IVF-conceived pregnancies: a retrospective study.
authors: Chen Y, Jiang P, Li X, Hu L, Li J, Chen Q, Gu Y
abstract: Pregnancies conceived using in vitro fertilization (IVF) significantly increase the risk of developing preeclampsia. One possible explanation is that embryos grown outside the body may implant differently compared to natural conceptions, potentially affecting placental development and increasing the risk of preeclampsia. Clinically, preeclampsia is classified into early-onset and late-onset forms, as well as severe and mild forms. Although some studies suggested that preeclampsia severity may be more pronounced in IVF-conceived pregnancies, the findings were controversial. In this retrospective study, we compared the severity of preeclampsia between naturally conceived and IVF-conceived pregnancies. A total of 498 preeclampsia cases were included, with 401 cases occurring in naturally conceived pregnancies and 97 in IVF-conceived pregnancies. The mean gestational age at delivery in the IVF-conceived group was 36 weeks, significantly earlier than that in the naturally conceived group (37 weeks, p = 0.0002). Additionally, 27 (28%) women in the IVF-conceived group developed early-onset preeclampsia, which was no statistical difference from the naturally conceived group (78, 19%, p = 0.0732). There was no significant difference in the proportion of severe preeclampsia between the two groups (16% vs. 23%, p = 0.1667). Additionally, gestational age at the onset of preeclampsia and the incidence of preterm birth were not different between the two groups after adjusting for important confounders, including maternal age, BMI, parity, and twin pregnancy. In conclusion, there is a known link between IVF conception and the increased risk of developing preeclampsia. Our study found that the severity of preeclampsia, once it occurred, did not differ between the two modes of conception.

title: Trends in research productivity among obstetrics and gynecology residency applicants in the United States: a national comparison across specialties, 2016 to 2024.
authors: Randall SE, Martinbianco E, Sadak K, Tjaden Peiffer AM
abstract: BACKGROUND: Research productivity has become an increasingly emphasised component of residency selection. However, longitudinal trends in obstetrics and gynecology (OB/GYN) applicant research output relative to other specialties remains poorly characterised, particularly in the context of evolving evaluation practices and the transition of USMLE Step 1 to pass/fail scoring. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate trends in research productivity among matched OB/GYN applicants and compare these patterns with other medical and surgical specialties from 2016 to 2024. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP) Charting Outcomes data from 2016-2024 was performed. Mean research experiences and research items (abstracts, posters, and publications) reported by matched applicants were extracted for each specialty and year. Descriptive longitudinal trend analyses were performed to evaluate changes over time. Mean research experiences and research items (abstracts, posters, and publications) were summarized by specialty and year, and linear trend lines were used to illustrate directional patterns. Comparisons with other specialties (all specialties, surgical specialties, and specialties with similar match rate ± 5%) were conducted descriptively. RESULTS: From 2016 to 2024, matched OB/GYN applicants saw increased mean research items (4.2 to 9.0; +114%) and research experiences (3.2 to 3.8; +19%). Growth in research output demonstrated upward trends across OB/GYN and other specialties, with increases observed across both surgical and non-surgical fields. Although unmatched applicants showed similar relative increases, matched applicants consistently reported higher absolute research output. CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS: OB/GYN applicants have increased their research output in recent years like other surgical and similarly competitive fields. As programs increasingly rely on scholarly metrics, educators and residency leaders should consider strategies to ensure equitable access to research opportunities and maintain holistic review practices during resident selection.

title: Hemodynamic effects of ventilating or not, during cardiopulmonary bypass in a porcine model.
authors: Kvalheim VL, Mongstad A, Husby P, Stangeland L, Nginamau ES, Osman TA, Yamada S, Grong K
abstract: Background. Optimal ventilator setting during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is unknown. Improved gas exchange and lung compliance have been suggested as favourable outcomes when lungs are ventilated. However, long-time effects have been hard to demonstrate. There has been less focus on the immediate circulatory effects of ventilator settings during cardioplegia and CPB, and potentially hemodynamic effects of different ventilator strategies are unknown. Methods. Sixteen anesthetized pigs on normothermic CPB with 80 min of aortic cross-clamp and cardioplegic arrest were randomized to a ventilated and a not ventilated group. After weaning, both cardiac-, hemodynamic-, and pulmonary functions were evaluated for up to 120 min. Results. Left ventricular variables and cardiac output did not differ between the two study groups, neither before nor after weaning. After weaning, mean pulmonary artery pressure was increased in ventilated compared to not ventilated animals. Neither pulmonary compliance nor oxygen uptake differed between groups in surviving animals. Conclusions. Disconnection of the ventilator during CPB and cardiac arrest did not affect lung compliance and oxygen uptake, neither positively nor negatively. In the ventilated group, a temporary increase in the pulmonary pressure after weaning was observed.

title: Clinical Outcomes following invasive coronary angiography for patients with acute coronary syndromes pretreated with P2Y12 inhibitors and considered for urgent coronary artery bypass graft surgery.
authors: Lim CJ, Singh M, Sammut MA, Faizur Rahman ME, Parker WAE, Sadeque SAA, Storey RF
abstract: This retrospective single-centre observational study included 262 sequential patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) undergoing invasive coronary angiography (ICA) while receiving P2Y12 inhibitors and considered for coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); P2Y12 inhibitors (ticagrelor 91%, thienopyridine 9%) were stopped prior to CABG. The primary outcome was recurrent myocardial infarction or death following ICA and prior to revascularisation or decision for conservative management. 2 patients (0.8%) had recurrent MI and died following ICA and prior to planned CABG, demonstrating a small risk of MI and death in patients who have delays to CABG following ICA for ACS.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: An optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched dual-crosslinkable hydrogel for cell-free remodeling of the corneal stroma.
authors: Wu W, Huai S, Li C, Wang L, Xie S, Lei L, Liu X, Wang J
abstract: Corneal trauma is a leading cause of visual impairment and blindness worldwide, yet corneal stromal repair and regeneration remain a significant challenge in ophthalmology because of its limited intrinsic repair capacity and fibrotic scar formation during healing process. Here we report an optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel that enables cell-free corneal stromal remodeling. By integrating dynamic covalent crosslinking with static photocrosslinking strategy, the optimized hydrogel-based substitute achieved high optical transparency, a refractive index of approximately 1.35, and an elastic modulus of 83.8 ± 13.4 kPa, closely resembling the properties of the healthy human cornea. In a rabbit model of deep corneal defects, the optimized in situ-forming hydrogel adapted to the defect geometry, adhered stably to the wound bed, recapitulated the optical and biomechanical properties of the native cornea, and supported scarless corneal stromal remodeling. Incorporation of the antimicrobial peptide HHC36 further endowed the hydrogel with robust antibacterial activity without compromising its optical and biomechanical properties. In a rabbit model of P. aeruginosa-infected deep corneal defects, the HHC36-loaded in situ-forming hydrogel effectively mitigated clinical signs of infection and substantially promoted corneal stromal remodeling within 30 days while reducing fibrosis. Overall, this optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel might be a promising substitute for corneal stromal remodeling.
